title: Read redirected SDK output with an explicit encoding
goal: Read non-ASCII SDK build diagnostics through a pipe using a declared UTF-8 decoder and the real exit code, when console code pages or proposed encoding opt-outs do not describe the observed bytes.

selectionNotes: Use an explicit UTF-8 reader for the verified Windows SDK build pipe. Default/false/true and source-level opt-out controls still emit UTF-8. No working legacy producer opt-out is claimed.
The SDK10 comparison reuses the existing reader; no newer-only reader API or ninth historical foundation.

platforms: Windows x64; redirected stdout/stderr, private CP1252/65001 consoles and en-US SDK UI language
prerequisites: Complete measured SDK10.0.402/runtime10.0.13 and SDK11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105/runtime11RC2 installations; PowerShell7.
Restore each pinned original project before the reader calls build --no-restore. No package, provider, workload or native compiler dependency for this route.
constraints: Real paired Windows x64 build/run, raw non-ASCII diagnostic bytes under private CP1252/65001 consoles; default/false/true and source opt-out controls, explicit UTF-8 decode, mismatched reader corruption and actual failed builds. No working legacy producer opt-out is qualified.
The SDK cannot discover a pipe reader encoding. Producer bytes and decoder policy must agree; code pages, glyph rendering and arbitrary tools are separate.
RC2 observations are not GA qualification. PIN-959/PIN-963/Human gates and exact eight foundations remain open.
stabilityLimitations: Evidence is .NET 11 RC2. Reconcile actual GA artifacts separately under PIN-963; no API taught here is designated experimental.
